core_topics: Data structures (arrays, hash maps, trees, graphs)
Software engineering practices (code review, testing, documentation)
red_flags: Cannot explain any past technical decision or why a choice was made
Dismisses testing or documentation as unnecessary
Cannot articulate a structured approach to debugging
No examples of learning from mistakes
Cannot describe a system at different levels of abstraction (high-level vs implementation)

calibration_examples.description: Thoughtful, structured, and backed by real experience. Proactively considers edge cases.
Demonstrates basic competency. Answers are correct but generic.
Vague, inconsistent, or lacks basic engineering fundamentals.

suggested_questions: Tell me about a technical project you're proud of. What problem did it solve and what were the key decisions?
Walk me through how you'd approach debugging a production issue affecting users right now.
How do you decide when code is good enough to ship versus needing more polish?
Describe a time you disagreed with a technical decision. How did you handle it?
How would you design a URL shortener service? Walk me through your thinking.
What's your approach to writing tests? What kinds of tests give you the most confidence?
Tell me about something you learned in the last 6 months that changed how you write code.
